stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Woodcut printing is one of the oldest ways to reproduce an image. The artist carves a design into a flat block of wood, cutting away every area that should stay white. The raised surface that remains ______ ink from a roller and transfers it to paper when the block is pressed down.
explanation: The subject of the last sentence is 'The raised surface.' The words 'that remains' only describe it, and 'remains' belongs to that small clause. So the subject still needs its own main verb. The blank also sits before 'and transfers,' so it has to match that verb. 'Picks up' is a tensed verb that matches 'transfers.' This is the first check you make on Easy questions where every choice is the same verb in a different form: does the subject already have a real verb?

A.why: 'Picking up' sounds smooth, but an -ing word can't be a sentence's main verb on its own. 'The raised surface... picking up ink' leaves the subject without a verb, and it doesn't match 'transfers' after 'and.'

B.why: You chose an infinitive. 'To pick up' names a purpose, not an action the subject performs, so the sentence still has no main verb before 'and transfers.'

D.why: 'Having picked up' is a nonfinite -ing form even though it uses 'having.' It describes something but doesn't give the subject a verb, so it can't be joined to 'transfers' with 'and.'

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Researchers who study endurance athletes often measure how much oxygen the body can use during hard exercise. In one common test, a runner ______ on a treadmill while the speed rises every two minutes. The test ends when the runner can no longer keep pace with the belt.
explanation: The subject of the middle sentence is 'a runner.' The verb 'rises' belongs to the 'while' clause, so it can't count as the runner's verb. The runner needs a tensed verb of its own, and 'runs' is the only choice that is one. Learning to set aside verbs that sit inside 'while,' 'when,' or 'that' clauses is what makes the real missing-verb questions quick to answer.

A.why: You probably counted 'rises' as the main verb. It belongs to the 'while' clause, so 'a runner running on a treadmill' still has no verb of its own, and the sentence is a fragment.

C.why: 'To run' is an infinitive. It can express a purpose, but it can't act as the main verb for 'a runner,' so the subject is left without one.

D.why: 'Having run' is a nonfinite form that describes an earlier action. It doesn't give 'a runner' a tensed verb, so the sentence is still incomplete.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Musicologists who study medieval chant face an unusual problem. The earliest surviving manuscripts ______ the rise and fall of each melody but not its exact pitches. Scholars must therefore reconstruct the notes by comparing these books with later copies written on a staff.
explanation: The subject of the second sentence is 'The earliest surviving manuscripts,' and there's no verb after it until the blank. The blank has to supply the main verb, and 'record' is the only tensed choice. On the exam this step comes first. Once you rule out every -ing and 'to' choice, the question is usually answered.

A.why: 'The earliest surviving manuscripts recording the rise and fall' reads like a full thought, but it's a fragment. An -ing word can describe the manuscripts but can't be their main verb.

B.why: An infinitive like 'to record' doesn't tell you what the manuscripts actually do. The subject still has no main verb, so the sentence isn't complete.

C.why: 'Having recorded' looks like it has a helping verb, but it's an -ing form, not a tensed verb. The manuscripts are still left without a main verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: At many excavation sites, archaeologists pour loose soil through screens made of fine wire mesh. The method ______ small objects such as beads, seeds, and fish bones, which would otherwise be missed. These finds often reveal more about daily life than larger artifacts do.
explanation: The subject of the second sentence is 'The method.' 'Would be missed' belongs to the 'which' clause, so it doesn't count. 'The method' still needs a main verb, and 'recovers' is the only tensed choice. This is the one skill behind the missing-verb questions on the Easy tier: find the subject, then check whether it has a real verb yet.

B.why: You may have counted 'would be missed' as the main verb. It belongs to the 'which' clause, so 'The method recovering small objects' still has no verb and is a fragment.

C.why: 'The method to recover small objects' names what the method is for. It never says what the method does, so the sentence has no main verb.

D.why: 'Having recovered' is nonfinite, so it can describe the method but can't serve as its verb. The subject is still left without one.
